name: Vowel Reverb
description: A hall whose tail sings: the reverb is shaped by the formants of a sung vowel, so what goes in comes back as a soft wordless choir.

params.name: Vowel
params.description: Which vowel the tail sings, from Ah through Eh, Ee and Oh to Oo. Settings in between are a mouth halfway from one vowel to the next.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: How strongly the vowel is pressed onto the reverb. At zero it is a plain hall; higher settings make the tail more vocal, and the vowel grows clearer the longer it rings.

params.name: Voice
params.description: The size of the singers, from a deep bass choir through tenor and alto to a bright soprano one.

params.name: Motion
params.description: Lets the vowel wander slowly towards its neighbours on its own, a little differently on each side, so the tail sounds like people singing instead of a fixed filter.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the sung notes of the tail take to die away. The sound between the vowel's resonances fades sooner as Resonance goes up.

params.name: Size
params.description: How big the room is, from a small chapel to a cathedral. Larger rooms answer later and more slowly. Moving it bends the pitch of the tail.

params.name: Pre-delay
params.description: The gap before the reverb starts, which keeps the start of the sound clear of the choir behind it.

params.name: Modulation
params.description: Slow pitch drift inside the reverb. A little makes the tail an ensemble of voices that are never quite in unison; a lot is a wide chorus.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Removes lows from the reverb so it does not cloud the bass. The dry signal is not touched.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Darkens the reverb. It also works inside the room, so the highs die away sooner than the rest.

params.name: Width
params.description: Stereo width of the reverb only. Zero is a mono tail; full is the widest.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the reverb. Fully up is the reverb alone.
